newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Neglected Belgian bonds seen awaiting sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Neglected Belgian bonds seen awaiting sell-off.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which floated higher in thin, desultory trade on Friday, are expected to continue bobbing in the wash of German Bunds for the rest of the year before selling emerges in January, traders said.
"It was hardly traded today. There was some end of year book cleaning but no one is interested," one trader said.
"There is no serious interest. All end-investors are on holiday. This could well have been the last active day of the year," another said.
However, traders said they expected the New Year to start with a bang as delayed profit-taking finally emerged.
"Everybody is long Belgium. I don't know one person who is short," one trader said.
Investors have been sitting on seriously large profits, not wanting to sell before the year-end for fear of being hit with major capital gains tax bills.
"They are all waiting and watching each other. The moment one goes, they all will," a trader said. "But everyone is scared to be the first."
Traders said there was nothing on the horizon to move the Belgian market, and even U.S. November durable goods orders and jobless claims due next Friday are seen having little impact.
